King County Washington Inmate Lookup

If you need to find information about someone in custody in King County, Washington, the King County Department of Adult and Juvenile Detention maintains an online inmate search database. A King County Washington inmate lookup allows family members, attorneys, and the public to locate inmates, check bail amounts, and find visitation information quickly and securely through official channels.

How to Search King County Jail Records

  1. Visit the official King County inmate search website — Go to the King County Department of Adult and Juvenile Detention's inmate information page. This is the primary resource maintained by the county and updated in real-time.
  2. Enter the inmate's name or booking number — Type the person's full name or their unique booking number into the search field. The system will return matching records with current custody status.
  3. Review the inmate's information — Once you locate the person, you'll see their booking date, charges, bail amount, next court date, and current housing location within the facility.
  4. Check visitation eligibility — The search results include information about whether the inmate is eligible for visits and any restrictions that may apply to your visit.
  5. Contact the jail directly for questions — If you cannot find the person or need additional details, call the King County jail's main line or visit in person during business hours for assistance.

Bail Bond Information for King County

When someone is arrested in King County, a bail amount is typically set during the arraignment hearing. Most bail bondsmen in the King County area charge a non-refundable fee of 10 percent of the total bail amount. For example, if bail is set at $10,000, you would pay a bondsman $1,000 to secure the defendant's release. This fee goes to the bail bond company and is separate from any bail amount posted directly to the court.

The timing of bail hearings in King County varies depending on the severity of charges and current court schedules. Typically, felony defendants must be brought before a judge within 72 hours of arrest for an initial appearance and bail determination. Many misdemeanor defendants are released on their own recognizance or with minimal bail. Having an attorney present at your bail hearing can significantly improve your chances of securing a lower bail amount or release without bail in King County.

Visitation Rules at King County Jail

  • Valid ID required — All visitors must present a government-issued photo identification, such as a driver's license or passport. Visitors without proper ID will be denied entry.
  • Visitation hours — King County jail typically allows visits during specific weekday and weekend hours. Check the facility's website or call ahead to confirm current visitation schedules, as hours may vary by housing unit.
  • Dress code — Visitors must dress appropriately and cannot wear revealing clothing, gang colors, or items that resemble jail uniforms. Hats, sunglasses, and certain accessories are prohibited inside the facility.
  • Video visitation available — If in-person visits are not possible, King County offers video visitation services through an online system, allowing remote communication with inmates from your home or computer.
  • Children visitation policy — Children under 18 may visit with advance approval and must be supervised by an adult at all times. Some housing units restrict or prohibit children's visits; contact the jail directly for specifics.

What to Expect After Arrest in King County

  1. Booking process — The arrestee is taken to the King County jail's booking area where personal information, charges, and mugshots are recorded. This process typically takes 1 to 3 hours.
  2. Medical screening — Staff conduct a brief medical evaluation to identify any urgent health conditions or medications needed during custody. Mental health screening is also performed at this stage.
  3. Classification assessment — Officers evaluate the inmate's background, charges, and behavior history to determine appropriate housing and custody level within the facility.
  4. Arraignment and bail hearing — Within 72 hours of arrest, the defendant appears before a judge for an initial appearance where charges are read and bail is set or the person is released.
  5. Transfer or release — If bail is paid or the person is released on their own recognizance, they are discharged. Otherwise, they are transferred to a housing unit to await trial or further court proceedings.

How to Contact King County Jail

If you have questions about an inmate or need additional information not available through the online search system, the King County Department of Adult and Juvenile Detention maintains phone lines and a physical address for public inquiries. Staff can help you locate someone, answer questions about visitation policies, and provide information about bail, charges, and court dates. It is best to call during business hours and have the inmate's full name or booking number ready when you contact them.

Frequently Asked Questions — King County Inmate Lookup

How do I find out if someone is in King County jail?

Use the official King County inmate search tool on the Department of Adult and Juvenile Detention website. Enter the person's full name or booking number, and the system will display their current custody status, charges, bail amount, and housing location if they are in the facility. You can also call the jail directly during business hours for assistance.

How long does booking take in King County?

The booking process at King County jail typically takes between 1 and 3 hours from the time of arrival. This includes recording personal information, taking mugshots, conducting medical and mental health screenings, and performing classification assessments. Complex cases or high volumes may extend this timeline. Once booking is complete, the inmate is assigned to a housing unit and becomes searchable in the online system.

Can I visit an inmate at King County jail?

Yes, visitation is generally allowed at King County jail during designated hours with advance approval in some cases. All visitors must present valid government-issued photo identification, follow dress code requirements, and comply with facility rules. Video visitation is also available if in-person visits are not convenient. Contact the jail or check their website to confirm current visitation schedules and any special restrictions.

What if the person is not in the county jail system?

If someone is not in King County jail, they may be housed in the Washington Department of Corrections, a different county facility, or a federal facility. Check the Washington DOC inmate locator and the Federal Bureau of Prisons website to search statewide and federal systems. You can also contact the King County Sheriff's Office to ask where the person was transferred or taken after arrest.

How do I send money to an inmate in King County?

King County jail offers multiple ways to send money to inmates for commissary, phone calls, and other expenses. You can typically send money through the official inmate account system via the jail's website, by phone, or in person at the facility. There may be processing fees depending on the method used. Contact King County jail directly for current options and instructions on depositing funds into an inmate's account.
